referenceCode:
def insert_kth(head, k, value):
    if k < 1:
        return head
    node = ListNode(value)
    if k == 1:
        node.next = head
        return node
    current = head
    index = 1
    while current is not None and index < k - 1:
        current = current.next
        index += 1
    if current is None:
        return head
    node.next = current.next
    current.next = node
    return head
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified singly linked-list test cases.

sourceTitle: Remove Nth node from the back of the LL
title: Remove Nth From the Back
description: Remove the node that is n positions from the end of the list and return the updated head. The replay should make the fast and slow cursors visible.
constraints: If n is larger than the list length, leave the list unchanged.
referenceCode:
def remove_nth_from_back(head, n):
    dummy = ListNode(0)
    dummy.next = head
    fast = dummy
    for step in range(n):
        if fast.next is None:
            return head
        fast = fast.next
    slow = dummy
    while fast.next is not None:
        fast = fast.next
        slow = slow.next
    slow.next = slow.next.next
    return dummy.next
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified singly linked-list test cases.

sourceTitle: Delete the middle node in LL
title: Delete the Middle Node
description: Delete the middle node of a singly linked list. When the list has an even length, delete the later middle node.
constraints: A zero- or one-node list becomes empty.
Use slow and fast pointers or an equivalent one-pass approach.
referenceCode:
def delete_middle(head):
    if head is None or head.next is None:
        return None
    slow = head
    fast = head
    previous = None
    while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:
        previous = slow
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
    previous.next = slow.next
    return head
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified singly linked-list test cases.

sourceTitle: Check if LL is palindrome or not
title: Check Linked List Palindrome
description: Return true if the linked-list values read the same forward and backward. The trace should show values being collected before comparison.
referenceCode:
def is_palindrome(head):
    values = []
    current = head
    while current is not None:
        values.append(current.val)
        current = current.next
    left = 0
    right = len(values) - 1
    while left < right:
        if values[left] != values[right]:
            return False
        left += 1
        right -= 1
    return True
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified singly linked-list test cases.

sourceTitle: Segregate odd and even nodes in Linked List
title: Group Odd Then Even Values
description: Return a list where nodes with odd values appear before nodes with even values, preserving the original relative order inside each group.
constraints: Odd/even is based on node value.
Reuse existing nodes so pointer rewires are visible.
referenceCode:
def group_odd_even_values(head):
    odd_dummy = ListNode(0)
    even_dummy = ListNode(0)
    odd_tail = odd_dummy
    even_tail = even_dummy
    current = head
    while current is not None:
        nxt = current.next
        current.next = None
        if current.val % 2 != 0:
            odd_tail.next = current
            odd_tail = current
        else:
            even_tail.next = current
            even_tail = current
        current = nxt
    odd_tail.next = even_dummy.next
    return odd_dummy.next if odd_dummy.next is not None else even_dummy.next
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified singly linked-list test cases.

sourceTitle: Sort a Linked List of 0's 1's and 2's
title: Sort Zero One Two List
description: The linked list contains only 0, 1, and 2 values. Return the list sorted so all 0s come first, then 1s, then 2s.
referenceCode:
def sort_zero_one_two(head):
    counts = [0, 0, 0]
    current = head
    while current is not None:
        counts[current.val] += 1
        current = current.next
    current = head
    value = 0
    while current is not None:
        while counts[value] == 0:
            value += 1
        current.val = value
        counts[value] -= 1
        current = current.next
    return head

sourceTitle: Rotate a Linked List
title: Rotate Linked List Right
description: Rotate the linked list to the right by k places and return the new head. The trace should show the tail reconnecting and the new tail being cut.
referenceCode:
def rotate_right(head, k):
    if head is None or head.next is None or k == 0:
        return head
    length = 1
    tail = head
    while tail.next is not None:
        tail = tail.next
        length += 1
    shift = k % length
    if shift == 0:
        return head
    tail.next = head
    steps_to_new_tail = length - shift
    new_tail = tail
    while steps_to_new_tail > 0:
        new_tail = new_tail.next
        steps_to_new_tail -= 1
    new_head = new_tail.next
    new_tail.next = None
    return new_head
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified singly linked-list test cases.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
description: Return the largest product of any non-empty contiguous subarray. The replay should show why both the best and worst running products matter.
constraints: The input has at least one integer.
referenceCode:
def max_product_subarray(nums):
    best = nums[0]
    high = nums[0]
    low = nums[0]
    for index in range(1, len(nums)):
        value = nums[index]
        if value < 0:
            temp = high
            high = low
            low = temp
        high = max(value, high * value)
        low = min(value, low * value)
        best = max(best, high)
    return best
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified one-dimensional array test cases.

sourceTitle: Kth element of 2 sorted arrays
title: Kth Element Across Two Sorted Arrays
description: Return the 1-indexed kth value from the merged order of two sorted arrays without asking the user to build the full answer.
constraints: Both arrays are sorted in nondecreasing order.
k is between 1 and the combined length of the arrays.
referenceCode:
def kth_sorted_value(nums1, nums2, k):
    i = 0
    j = 0
    taken = 0
    answer = 0
    while taken < k:
        if j >= len(nums2) or (i < len(nums1) and nums1[i] <= nums2[j]):
            answer = nums1[i]
            i += 1
        else:
            answer = nums2[j]
            j += 1
        taken += 1
    return answer
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified sorted-array merge cases.

title: Add Two Linked-List Numbers
description: Each list stores a number in reverse digit order. Return a new linked list holding the sum in the same reverse order.
constraints: Each node stores one digit from 0 through 9.
Either input list may be empty.

starterCode:

    return list1 or list2
referenceCode:
def add_two_numbers(list1, list2):
    dummy = ListNode(0)
    tail = dummy
    carry = 0
    a = list1
    b = list2

    while a is not None or b is not None or carry:
        total = carry
        if a is not None:
            total += a.val
            a = a.next
        if b is not None:
            total += b.val
            b = b.next
        carry = total // 10
        tail.next = ListNode(total % 10)
        tail = tail.next

    return dummy.next
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified reverse-digit linked-list cases.

sourceTitle: Reverse LL in group of given size K
title: Reverse Linked List in K-Groups
description: Reverse every complete group of k nodes and leave the final shorter group untouched. Pointer rewires should be visible in the replay.
constraints: Only complete groups of k nodes are reversed.
Return the head of the updated list.
referenceCode:
def reverse_k_group(head, k):
    if k <= 1 or head is None:
        return head

    dummy = ListNode(0)
    dummy.next = head
    group_prev = dummy

    while True:
        kth = group_prev
        for _ in range(k):
            kth = kth.next
            if kth is None:
                return dummy.next

        group_next = kth.next
        prev = group_next
        current = group_prev.next
        while current is not group_next:
            nxt = current.next
            current.next = prev
            prev = current
            current = nxt

        old_group_head = group_prev.next
        group_prev.next = kth
        group_prev = old_group_head
reviewNotes: Original Noesis wording and hand-verified singly linked-list rewiring cases.
